newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Peace negotiators mull future of Guatemalan rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peace negotiators mull future of Guatemalan rebels.

text.p: Government and rebel peace negotiators could sign an accord regarding the future of Guatemalan guerrillas by the end of October, a government official said on Monday.

After a three-day meeting last week in Mexico City, negotiators agreed to two more October negotiating sessions to discuss the political future of the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG in Spanish).

Gustavo Porras, the top government peace negotiator, told reporters on Monday that a final peace agreement putting 11 separate accords, most of them already signed, into effect was still on track for ratification in December.
The United Nations has moderated sporadic Guatemalan peace negotations since 1991, but talks picked up earlier this year with a ceasefire and the signing of an important land and labour accord.
Three weeks ago rebels and the government signed a landmark agreement in Mexico City, reducing Guatemala's powerful army by a third and limiting its post-war role.

The URNG is an umbrella group of four guerrilla fronts, formed in 1982, one of the most violent periods during Guatemala's 36-year civil war which has left an estimated 100,000 dead and 40,000 missing.
Porras said negotiators will consider proposals for training and employment programmes to facilitate the return of rebels to a legal civilian life.
